h1: English CEFR Level Progression: Hours & Timeline Calculator
description: Enter your current CEFR level (A1–C1) and weekly study hours — get the exact weeks to your next level and total hours to C1. Based on Cambridge English research. Includes a full A1–C2 hours table.
answerSnippet: According to Cambridge English research, reaching C1 from A1 requires approximately 1,050 guided study hours: ~150 h (A1→A2), ~200 h (A2→B1), ~300 h (B1→B2), and ~400 h (B2→C1). At 10 hours/week, that is roughly 105 weeks (~2 years). Each level requires progressively more time — B2→C1 alone is ~400 hours.
intro: This calculator shows exactly how many weeks it takes to advance from your current English CEFR level to the next one — and how many total hours remain until you reach C1 (Advanced). It uses the Cambridge English cumulative guided-hour benchmarks (A1 → A2 → B1 → B2 → C1 → C2) cross-referenced with US Foreign Service Institute (FSI) data. The formula divides the transition hours for your level by the weekly hours you study. For example, a B1 learner studying 7 hours/week needs ~300 hours to reach B2 — about 43 weeks. Use this to plan a Cambridge exam timeline (PET, FCE, CAE), set Duolingo supplement hours, or map out a realistic path to professional-level English.
keyTakeaway: **Weeks to Next Level = Transition Hours ÷ Hours Per Week.** Cambridge benchmarks: B1→B2 ≈ 300 h; B2→C1 ≈ 400 h. A B1 learner at 10 h/week reaches B2 in **~30 weeks**, and C1 in **~70 weeks (~16 months)**.
useCases: A university student at B1 planning to take the Cambridge FCE (B2) exam in 9 months wants to know the minimum weekly study hours required.
A professional relocating abroad who is currently at A2 needs to reach B2 for a visa language requirement and wants a realistic self-study timeline.
A Duolingo user who finished the English tree wants to cross-reference their streak with CEFR hours to estimate their true proficiency level.
A language school coordinator building a course schedule needs to assign the correct number of instructional weeks per CEFR band for accreditation.
A high school student preparing for a gap year program requiring B2 English wants to know weekly tutoring hours needed from A2.

explanation:
## Hours Required Per CEFR Level — Reference Table

Based on **Cambridge English** cumulative guided learning hour research, widely cited by accredited language institutions.

| From | To | Transition Hours | Cumulative from A0 | Cambridge Exam |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A0 (Beginner) | A1 | ~100 h | ~100 h | — |
| A1 | A2 | ~150 h | ~250 h | Cambridge A2 Key (KET) |
| A2 | B1 | ~200 h | ~450 h | Cambridge B1 Preliminary (PET) |
| B1 | B2 | ~300 h | ~750 h | Cambridge B2 First (FCE) |
| B2 | C1 | ~400 h | ~1,150 h | Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) |
| C1 | C2 | ~200 h | ~1,350 h | Cambridge C2 Proficiency (CPE) |

**Key insight:** Each successive level takes more time. B2→C1 (400 h) requires more than A0→B1 (450 h combined). Higher levels demand 10,000+ word vocabulary depth, academic register, and complex grammar nuance.

---

## Timeline at Different Study Intensities

For a **B1 learner aiming for C1** (700 hours of transition study needed):

| Hours/Week | Weeks to B2 (300 h) | Weeks to C1 (700 h) | Approx. Time to C1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 h/week | 100 weeks | 234 weeks | ~4.5 years |
| 5 h/week | 60 weeks | 140 weeks | ~2.7 years |
| 7 h/week | 43 weeks | 100 weeks | ~23 months |
| 10 h/week | 30 weeks | 70 weeks | ~16 months |
| 15 h/week | 20 weeks | 47 weeks | ~11 months |
| 20 h/week (intensive) | 15 weeks | 35 weeks | ~8 months |

---

## How the Calculator Works

```
Weeks to Next Level = TransitionHours[currentLevel] ÷ hoursPerWeek
Total Hours to C1 = Sum of all transition hours from current level to C1

Example (B1 → C1, 5 h/week):
  B1→B2 transition = 300 h → 300 ÷ 5 = 60 weeks
  B2→C1 transition = 400 h → 400 ÷ 5 = 80 weeks
  Total to C1 = 700 h → 700 ÷ 5 = 140 weeks (~2.7 years)
```

**What counts as a "guided hour":** Active focused study — classes, structured self-study with exercises, tutoring sessions, or mock exams. Passive exposure (background TV, casual podcast listening) counts at roughly 25–33% efficiency. Duolingo sessions average 10–15 min and should be counted at 50–60% value due to the gamified format.

---

## Duolingo vs. Structured Study

A **daily 15-min Duolingo habit** = 1.75 h/week of app time, but only ~0.9 effective guided hours/week after quality adjustment. At that rate, a B1 learner would need:
- B2: 300 h ÷ 0.9 = **333 weeks (~6.4 years)** on Duolingo alone
- Supplement with 2 h/week of structured study → effective 2.9 h/week → **~103 weeks (~2 years)** to B2

Duolingo is best as a vocabulary maintenance tool, not a standalone path to B2+.

---

## FSI Language Difficulty & Your Native Language

The US FSI rates English difficulty for native speakers of other languages (and vice versa). If your native language is:
- **Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese** (Category I): the hour estimates above apply directly
- **German, Dutch, Scandinavian** (Category II): multiply estimates by ~1.1–1.2×
- **Russian, Greek, Polish, Turkish** (Category III): multiply by ~1.4–1.6×
- **Arabic, Chinese, Japanese, Korean** (Category IV): multiply by ~1.8–2.2×

---

## Common Mistakes

1. **Counting passive hours as full study hours.** Netflix in English or background podcasts = 25–40% efficiency versus active recall practice (Modern Language Association estimate).
2. **Assuming all CEFR jumps take the same time.** B2→C1 requires more hours than A0→B1 combined.
3. **Conflating Duolingo crowns with CEFR levels.** Completing the Duolingo English tree typically maps to A2–B1 in receptive skills, with weaker productive skills (writing, speaking).
4. **Forgetting that study consistency beats total hours.** 1 hour/day × 5 days beats 5 hours Saturday due to the Ebbinghaus spaced-repetition effect.

faq.q: How many hours does it take to go from A1 to C1 in English?
faq.a: According to Cambridge English research, advancing from A1 to C1 requires approximately **1,000–1,050 guided study hours** in total: ~150 h (A1→A2) + ~200 h (A2→B1) + ~300 h (B1→B2) + ~400 h (B2→C1). At 10 hours/week, that is about 100–105 weeks, or roughly **2 years of consistent study**.

faq.q: How many hours per week do I need to pass Cambridge FCE (B2 First) in one year from B1?
faq.a: The B1→B2 transition requires approximately **300 guided hours**. One year is ~52 weeks, so: `300 ÷ 52 ≈ 5.8 h/week`. A practical schedule: 2 hours of class/tutoring + 4 hours of self-study per week. Cambridge recommends including at least one mock exam monthly in the final 3 months to build exam stamina.

faq.q: What is CEFR and how do the levels A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2 compare?
faq.a: CEFR (Common European Framework of Reference) is the international standard for language proficiency. A1–A2 = basic user (survival phrases, simple conversations); B1–B2 = independent user (travel, professional contexts, academic study); C1–C2 = proficient user (near-native fluency, complex academic/professional discourse). Cambridge exams map directly: A2 Key → B1 Preliminary → B2 First (FCE) → C1 Advanced (CAE) → C2 Proficiency (CPE).

faq.q: Do Duolingo hours count as full study hours?
faq.a: No, at full value. Duolingo averages 10–15 min/session and is optimized for vocabulary and basic grammar — CEFR assessments consistently place Duolingo completers at A2–B1 in receptive skills, lower in productive skills. For this calculator, count Duolingo time at **50–60% efficiency** versus tutored or classroom hours. A 20 min/day Duolingo habit = roughly 0.8–1.1 effective guided hours/week.

faq.q: What is the difference in hours between B1 and B2 English?
faq.a: The B1→B2 transition (from Intermediate to Upper-Intermediate) requires approximately **300 guided study hours** per Cambridge English benchmarks. This is the most common target level for professionals, visa requirements, and university entry. At 5 h/week that is 60 weeks; at 10 h/week it is 30 weeks (~7 months).

faq.q: How long does it take to reach B2 English from A2?
faq.a: From A2 to B2 requires two level transitions: A2→B1 (~200 h) + B1→B2 (~300 h) = **~500 guided hours** total. At 8 h/week: 500 ÷ 8 = **~62 weeks (~15 months)**. At 12 h/week (intensive): 500 ÷ 12 = **~42 weeks (~10 months)**.

faq.q: Is C1 English required for US university admission?
faq.a: Most US universities accept TOEFL iBT 80–100 (≈ B2–C1) or IELTS 6.5–7.0 for undergraduate admission. Ivy League and top-tier programs often require TOEFL 100+ or IELTS 7.5+, corresponding to solid C1. IELTS score mapping: 6.0–6.5 ≈ B2; 7.0–8.0 ≈ C1. Always verify requirements directly with each institution.

faq.q: Does my native language affect how long it takes to learn English?
faq.a: Yes, significantly. The FSI rates language-learning difficulty for English speakers and vice versa. Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese speakers typically need 600–750 hours to reach B2–C1 in English (Category I). Arabic, Chinese, Japanese, Korean speakers may need 1,100–1,400+ hours for equivalent English proficiency — roughly a 1.5–2× multiplier on the standard estimates.

faq.q: Can immersion abroad shorten the time to reach B2 or C1?
faq.a: Yes, substantially. Full immersion converts passive daily exposure into active input. Studies on immersion language acquisition suggest learners gain the equivalent of **1.5–2× guided classroom hours** per actual hour spent communicating professionally in the target language. A B1 learner working full-time in an English-speaking country can realistically reach B2 in 12–18 months versus 2–3 years of home-country study at 5 h/week.
